title: Deployment QA wait and connection recovery
summary: The driver executes server-selected pending plans outside bounded dispatch threads, preserving its acting session and candidate checkout. Target digests isolate live groups in one session. It polls QA facts, dispatches on change, and gives the final deadline dispatch a normal poll interval. Review and manual evidence stay waiting while other groups run. Recovery commands name the selected connection and run. Older serving replies without pending plans retain notice-based recovery. When the driver exits at the wait, control-plane upkeep sends each unsent, addressable item-QA member its stage-wait notice under the driver's own key, so no re-drive is needed to wake it; the fleet report shows that member as wake pending until it does. A member whose live execution has a live owner is skipped by the driver and upkeep alike, which share one open-walk rule; the fleet report reads it as 'walking under session S', 'queued for <machine>, <place>' when its execution waits for a Test Machine, or handed back for review, and its case lines name that execution instead of a run recipe. Each run row counts its members ('item QA: N open: walking, queued, not started, red'); the run is marked as needing action only for a red member, a member no walk covers and nobody can wake, or a run-level wait with no driver. A walking mission names the walk, not review commands, until hand-back.
